title: Transverse Aortic Constriction Procedure in Mice
author: Mark Kelly
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.56ig9ce

steps.title: Administer Pre-surgical Analgesics
steps.instruction: Approximately 30 minutes prior to the surgical procedure, administer subcutaneous (S.C.) injections of Buprenorphine (0.05mg/kg) and Meloxicam (5mg/kg).

steps.title: Anesthetize the Mouse
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the mouse using either Ketamine (80-100mg/kg) and Xylazine (5-20mg/kg) or Isoflurane (1-3%).

substeps.instruction: Assess depth of anesthesia at the start of the procedure using a toe or ear pinch.
Continue visual monitoring and toe/ear pinches throughout the procedure, noting any deviations from expected behavior.

steps.title: Prepare the Surgical Site
steps.instruction: Prepare the mouse for surgery using aseptic techniques.

substeps.instruction: Position the mouse supine on a heating pad.
Shave the fur around the incision site, specifically the ventral neck and left parasternal area.
Prep the surgical field with 70% isopropanol and Betadine solution, then drape.

steps.title: Expose the Sternum
steps.instruction: Perform a longitudinal midline cervical incision from the supra-sternal notch to the mid-chest to expose the sternum.

steps.title: Retract Thyroid and Dissect Muscles
steps.instruction: Clear the surgical field to access the chest cavity.

substeps.instruction: Pass a 6-0 Prolene stay suture through the thyroid and tape it to the sterile working area.
Bluntly dissect pre-tracheal muscles with micro-surgical forceps to expose the trachea.
Continue blunt dissection under the pre-tracheal muscles and behind the sternum to move the pleura away.

steps.title: Perform Partial Sternotomy
steps.instruction: Create an opening in the upper sternum for access.

substeps.instruction: Gently elevate the right supra-clavicular muscles with forceps.
Perform a 3-4 mm upper partial sternotomy by cutting the upper sternum.
Secure the opening using a retractor or by placing a 6-0 Prolene stay suture through each side and taping it to the sterile working area.

steps.title: Visualize the Aortic Arch
steps.instruction: Expose the aortic arch while avoiding damage to the parietal pleura to prevent pneumothorax.

substeps.instruction: Move aside the pre-tracheal muscles, mediastinal fat, and thymus.

steps.title: Perform Transverse Aortic Constriction (TAC)
steps.instruction: Constrict the aorta using a suture and a cannula needle.

substeps.instruction: Bluntly dissect soft tissue under the aortic arch and prepare a tunnel.
Pass a segment of 5-0 silk suture under the aorta between the innominate and left common carotid arteries.
Place a 27g cannula needle alongside the aorta.
Tie the suture snugly around the needle and the aorta between the right innominate and left common carotid arteries.
Quickly but gently remove the needle to achieve a ~0.4 mm diameter narrowing (65-70% aortic constriction).

steps.title: Close the Surgical Site
steps.instruction: Remove all stay sutures and close the surgical site using 6-0 Prolene sutures.

steps.title: Post-operative Care and Monitoring
steps.instruction: Provide analgesia and monitor the mice following the procedure.

substeps.instruction: Administer Buprenorphine (0.05mg/kg) every 12 hours for 72 hours post-op.
Administer Meloxicam (5mg/kg) every 24 hours for 72 hours post-op.
Monitor mice 2x daily for the first 72 hours, then at least 3x per week thereafter.

steps.title: Verify Stenosis
steps.instruction: One day following the TAC procedure, subject the mouse to Doppler echocardiography to determine the degree of induced stenosis.
